title: A condition is judged by PHP's full truthy table; every other `bool` position stays checked
scope:
the exact set of syntax positions that test a value's truthiness rather than requiring it
already be `bool` — `if`/`elseif`'s condition, `while`/`do…while`'s condition, `for`'s middle clause, the
ternary/elvis operator's condition, and `&&`/`||`/`!`'s operand(s); the runtime rule those positions use to
turn an arbitrary value into a branch decision.

summary.headline: `if ($rows)` works: a condition uses PHP’s truthy table, nothing else does
summary.body:
In an `if`, `while` or `for`, a ternary, or an operand of `&&`, `||` and `!`, any value may
stand alone and is judged as PHP judges it: `null`, `false`, `0`, `0.0`, `""` and `"0"` are
false, an empty array is false, and everything else — every object, closure and enum case, every
non-empty array — is true. A `bytes` value is false only when empty. Those positions are the
whole list: a `bool` parameter, property or return, and `==` or `match`, still need an explicit
`as bool` or a comparison.
